title: Heat From Cremations Is Being Used to Warm Homes and Swimming Pools
gist: European crematoria increasingly sell or reuse waste heat (Redditch pool since 2013, Aberdeen school, a Finnish all-electric crematorium tied to district heating), but the resource is small (about 1% of UK heat demand) and hard to replicate in the US where district heat is rare.

insights.claim: Redditch Borough Council has heated a local swimming pool with crematorium heat since 2013, saving tens of thousands of pounds a year in fuel, after a 2011 public backlash faded.
insights.speaker: Chris Baraniuk
insights.so_what: Waste-heat reuse can be economic when a large thermal sink is nearby.
insights.locator: Eventually, the relentless press coverage faded away

insights.claim: An Aberdeen school under construction will get just under 1 GWh of crematorium heat annually, about half its requirement, with a heat pump covering the rest and full operation by February 2027.
insights.speaker: Chris Baraniuk
insights.so_what: Pairing waste heat with heat pumps is a replicable template for public buildings.
insights.locator: The crematorium will provide just under 1 gigawatt-hour

insights.claim: A fully electric crematorium opening in Kangasala, Finland, in 2028 will connect to a district heat network serving more than 6,500 homes, driven by a push to cut natural gas after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Chris Baraniuk
insights.so_what: Geopolitics is pushing Nordic heat networks to absorb unusual waste-heat sources.
insights.locator: The crematorium that will open in Kangasala, Finland, in 2028

insights.claim: A 2024 study estimated that tapping every UK crematorium for waste heat would meet only about 1 percent of the country's heating needs.
insights.speaker: Chris Baraniuk
insights.so_what: Niche resource; do not expect material impact on heating decarbonization.

insights.claim: US adoption is harder because district heat networks are rare and crematoria are privately owned, raising the investment needed for heat exchangers and piping; Matthews Environmental Solutions is watching until economics align.
insights.speaker: Chris Baraniuk
insights.so_what: A US market would need district-heat build-out first; Matthews is a potential supplier.
insights.locator: implementing heat recovery tech at crematoria in the US is more difficult

insights.claim: A Quebec funeral complex has used cremation heat exchangers for over a decade, saving an estimated 29 metric tons of greenhouse gas emissions annually.
insights.speaker: Chris Baraniuk
insights.so_what: Small absolute savings show the modest scale of the opportunity.

insights.claim: A gas-fired cremation emits around 250 kg of carbon, and heat recovery offsets some of it (one company claims 100 kg) but not all.
insights.speaker: Chris Baraniuk
insights.so_what: Electrification matters more than recovery alone for decarbonizing the sector.
insights.locator: The carbon intensity of cremation varies

insights.claim: Crematoria are cutting energy via software that schedules oven firing to services and by batching coffins held up to 72 hours.
insights.speaker: Chris Baraniuk
insights.so_what: Operational efficiency is an adjacent software and services opportunity.
insights.locator: software can schedule the firing of gas ovens
